operations.comment: ; iNES header: 32 KiB PRG, 32 KiB CHR, mapper 3 and vertical mirroring. This is file metadata, not CPU
; code.
; Preserve X/Y, latch controller 1, and read its held/new buttons. Outside demo mode also retain the
; old decoded mat mask and sample the mat on port 2.
; Combine the two controller data bits over eight serial reads; publish held buttons and rising edges
; against the previous sample.
; Scan sixteen port-2 bits through the routing table, then pack three accumulators into the decoded
; mat mask and auxiliary bits. This requires the floor mat peripheral.
; A nonzero sampled sensor selects a destination byte and bit mask from the routing table. Y advances
; for every sensor, including inactive ones.
; Sixteen sensor-routing bytes: low two bits select one of the scan accumulators; the remaining bits
; encode its destination mask. ReadFloorMat visits all sixteen entries.
; Multiply input A by X using shift/add. Return the 16-bit product in X:Y (high:low); scratch $10-$12
; is destroyed.
; Preserve task X and compare the player collision record with four records spaced eight bytes apart.
; A bounds the record count; X is the first collision record and Y the candidate. Only negative active
; records participate; advance Y by eight.
; Compare absolute separations with combined extents on both axes; optionally compare the extra depth
; field. Overlap toggles flags $81 in both records and returns carry clear.
; Shift an eight-byte state with XOR feedback from bit 1 of the first two bytes. This is the game's
; pseudo-random source, not an input decoder.
; Use the menu substate to initialize title/options, accept mode and event selections, or enter the
; event lifecycle. Demo timeout selects successive events.
; Start accepts the current mode; Select cycles three modes. A periodic idle counter enters a rotating
; event demonstration.
; Transition through the intermediate selection screens, then allow Select to cycle five events and
; Start to begin.
; Clear demo/menu state, hide sprites, reset event counters and random seed, then allocate the player
; task.
; Combine selection A and group X with parallel coordinate tables; blink by choosing the alternate
; sprite descriptor and draw two sprites.
; Parallel menu-marker coordinate tables and sprite constants. DrawSelectionMarker combines group and
; choice indices; these bytes are not callable entries.
; Count active event frames, handle Start/pause, and process event exit. Normal progression advances
; through five events, then results/certificate according to mode and score.
; Disable rendering, select the menu CHR request, clear nametables and sound, and reset scroll/control
; shadows for a fresh screen.
; Remove six task slots, starting at slot zero. The shared loop also supports a caller-supplied start
; slot and count.
; Remove X consecutive task slots starting with Y; called by full-screen reset and event completion.
; On a new Start edge, suspend audio and blink the pause sprite while polling input and waiting for
; NMI; resume audio and hide that sprite on the next Start edge.
; Clear the display, draw an ordinal derived from completed rounds and queue the award script; wait
; before clearing again.
; A zero-terminated PPU command script queued by ShowCourseAward; ExecutePpuScript defines its packed
; destination/count encoding.
; Clamp event score to 100, store it by event, and add to the 16-bit total. Also accumulate half of
; the course-distance counter.
; Derive capped aggregate scores, build five adjusted event ratings, and draw decimal values. Integer
; division uses repeated subtraction with explicit rounding.
; Draw the last event score at the supplied origin and sprite slot. Suppress it for event flag bit 1
; or scores at least 100; one-digit scores get a leading decoration, followed by the decimal digits
; and trailing descriptor.
; A holds a value with bit 7 controlling leading-zero suppression; Y selects a three-sprite template.
; Split into decimal digits and emit the required sprite count.
; Three four-byte sprite templates for decimal output. Each descriptor stores relative Y, relative X,
; tile and attributes; the digit helper changes tile indices.
; Clear screen-initialized state, then run the shared screen dispatcher.
; On first entry hide sprites, clear PPU/sound, select one of six six-byte records, queue its script
; and tail-dispatch through the record handler. Later calls use its continuation state.
; Initialize certificate fields, select the award script/rank, draw its number and append two rank
; tiles to the dynamic PPU queue. Wait for any new button edge.
; Paired certificate rank tiles, selected after rank calculation; the dynamic queue writes one
; adjacent pair. This range is non-code; not every value has a separately established rank name.
; Preserve A as a button mask across frame waits; return when a new button edge intersects it. Zero
; mask would wait forever.
; Draw ten title sprites from coordinate arrays, hide four unused positions, and draw the remaining
; title decoration.
; Title sprite descriptors and coordinate arrays. RenderTitleSprites uses ten coordinate pairs plus a
; separate decoration sequence.
; Draw five four-byte sprite descriptors at zero origin using the shared sprite sequence helper.
; Five four-byte event-choice sprite descriptors: relative Y, relative X, tile and attributes.
; Compute result categories, reveal messages with timed waits, then wait a bounded interval or until a
; held button shortens it.
; Read category X from scratch results and queue its message only when below the category's limit.
; Alternate entry takes category A directly.
; A is the already-selected category and X its message group; enforce the group limit before indexing
; paired script pointers.
; Partition total score, find strongest/weakest event and their spread, and select message categories.
; A zero total suppresses dependent messages with $FF.
; Result message pointer pairs, group offsets, final-message selectors and category bounds.
; QueueResultCategoryValue checks each category before indexing the message words.
; Six six-byte screen records: control, palette, PPU script low/high, handler low/high. ScreenSelector
; is established as 0..5 by menu/completion callers; the dispatcher multiplies by six.
; Initialize editable fields and PPU scripts once, then update cursor, blink and controller-driven
; profile entry each frame.
; X selects five four-byte records: RAM destination word followed by two initialization bytes. Writes
; are indirect into RAM.
; Five-field initialization records store destination low/high plus two bytes to write. Adjacent
; reset/profile defaults share this non-code range; exact internal subtable limits are not all
; asserted.
; Choose grid dimensions for the active field; process new buttons immediately and held directional
; input at a repeat interval. Cursor indices wrap within the selected grid.
; Insert a selected character, update field length and advance fields when their limits are reached.
; The first field has a separate selection confirmation path.
; Choose one of two PPU scripts from the profile selector; negative selection is ignored and the
; accepted selection is retained in RAM.
; Compare the active field's limit with current length; carry reports whether the limit has been
; reached.
; Erase the current cursor cell and advance its character index through the shared field-length path.
; Remove a character or move to the preceding field when already at its start; prevent the field index
; from becoming negative.
; Small profile field limits and selector constants. The entry UI uses different grid dimensions and
; length limits for each field.
; Erase the old cursor and select the next field.
; Select PPU destination and RAM buffer pointers from parallel word tables; reset grid cursor and
; assign the supplied character index.
; Reset screen state and derive a numeric profile value from two stored digits. Two $FF bytes select a
; default value of ten.
; Parallel words for profile PPU destinations and RAM buffers, followed by selection scripts. These
; are CPU pointers/PPU command bytes, not bank-switch values.
; Convert grid row/column to screen coordinates, adjusting for field layout, then draw one cursor
; sprite.
; One four-byte cursor sprite descriptor, passed to DrawSprite as relative Y/X, tile and attributes.
; Flatten row*14+column and select the alphabet table appropriate to the active field.
; At eight-frame intervals, alternate the cursor tile between blank and marker and append a dynamic
; PPU update.
; Use the blank tile and shared cell-write path with a field-dependent PPU address adjustment.
; Store A through the active RAM buffer pointer and derive its PPU destination from the field address
; and character index.
; Unknown physical $0BDE..$0BE0: bytes encode LDY #0, but an optional queue-preparation entry and data
; remain competing interpretations. No selected entry or independent structural contract is
; established.
; Append destination high/low, count/flags and one tile to the dynamic queue; maintain a zero
; terminator and queue length.
; Map an unset $FF digit to zero; other values pass through unchanged.
; Clear background/sprite enable bits in the mask shadow; if no palette update is pending, request a
; temporary palette update and wait for NMI.
; Set background/sprite enable bits and ensure the last palette is requested before waiting for NMI.
; PPU scripts, text/alphabet data and menu tile layouts. Scripts encode destination high/low and
; packed count/flags, with optional stride/repetition; a zero destination-high terminates. Reviewed
; consumer/pattern evidence supports non-code, without claiming that all 2,461 bytes form one script
; or a fully recovered text encoding.
; Initialize the course strip buffers once; subsequently compare current and previous scroll and
; stream a new strip whenever a four-pixel boundary is crossed.
; Fill attribute work buffers and event-specific blank values, request a bottom-area fill, and wait
; two frames before use.
; Event-indexed attribute fills and bottom-area tile selections used by InitializeCourseBuffers. Five-
; event selectors are established; unrelated padding/extra values have no invented event names.
; Construct eleven course strips around the initial scroll, alternating nametables on wrap. Retain
; front/back strip cursors for incremental streaming.
; Use a course index times twelve to locate paired block IDs. Decode tile pointers and combine their
; attribute nibbles into six packed bytes; request NMI tile upload.
; Only act when scroll bit 2 changes. Check the forward frontier, decode the newly exposed strip and
; update its nametable/attribute destination and frontier.
; Mirror forward streaming using the rear frontier. Handle nametable wrap and request the reverse-
; direction upload path.
; Block ID selects a seventeen-byte record: sixteen tile indices and a final attribute selector.
; Resolve two tile values and the selected attribute byte; preserve registers.
; Resolve four tile IDs to four-byte descriptors, copy paired tile columns to the strip buffers, and
; preserve register state.
; Copy two rows from each of two descriptor pointers into four parallel tile-strip buffers at X.
; Same paired-copy layout as the other entry; kept separately because both physical routines are
; called by the strip builder.
; Multiply tile ID by four and add the event descriptor base to form one of four scratch pointers
; selected by Y.
; Preserve A/X/Y. Resolve DecodedTile0/1 into two tile pairs and copy them at strip position
; 2*StripByteIndex-2 and the following position. Requires initialized descriptor/strip buffers; no
; natural caller is established.
; Repeated sixteen-byte $10/$11 runs followed by sparse count/zero records. Bounded inspection of
; neighboring strip resolvers and copies establishes non-code here, but not a complete record format
; or a specific consumer for every byte.
; Initialize player/event state once, then dispatch the movement state machine from mat input, course
; conditions and collision tests. Demo input comes from timed byte streams.
; State 5 pushes the stored high/low continuation bytes and RTS transfers to stored-address-plus-one.
; The installed recovery/start/finish chains below use this same entry-minus-one convention.
; Prioritize end-of-event, collision recovery, stored continuation and special movement states before
; interpreting the current mat mask.
; Choose a movement entry from exact decoded mat patterns and event type. Similar patterns share setup
; helpers; other combinations use the fallback action.
; Configure masks $80/$40 and a unit variant; set the player motion-side flag.
; Use the upper mat pair but change the auxiliary mask to eight.
; Configure masks $04/$02 and unit variant; clear the player motion-side flag.
; Use the lower mat pair but change the auxiliary mask to eight.
; Demo mask lookup plus five timed mat streams. A stream byte uses low three bits as a pattern
; selector and high five as duration; zero inserts a 30-tick idle and $FF ends the demonstration.
; Exact per-stream extents are not independently asserted.
; Interpret the previous mat pattern when all sensors are released; choose recovery/action animation
; or a delayed idle path based on course conditions.
; Clear the pose-offset flag and join the common movement/collision commit path.
; Set the pose-offset flag before common scroll, progress and collision processing.
; Apply signed scroll delta, update course progress and visible objects, then refresh the player
; collision record and test overlaps.
; Copy player screen coordinates, assign collision extents and apply pose-dependent horizontal
; offsets; publish active flags for collision testing.
; Compare the previous mask with configured pair masks, update rhythm counter and choose a base
; animation or alternate stepping state.
; For wide pose IDs, adjust screen position and motion before selecting the new animation; preserve
; animation selection X.
; For side pose IDs, apply paired movement adjustments before choosing the new animation; preserve X.
; Reset scroll delta, recognize previous pair/auxiliary masks, normalize side position and select a
; first-side pose.
; Handle single low-side input, set lateral position, and reconnect to paired-step logic when the
; opposite side was previously active.
; Mirror first-side handling for the other mat side; normalize lateral position and choose the
; corresponding pose.
; Mirror the single-side transition, including Hop-a-Log-specific position adjustment.
; Store the selected crossing mask and pose, clear transient offsets and draw the crossed-input
; animation.
; Play the step sound, clear continuation and select a first-side stepping animation; enter movement
; state 1 or its mirrored variant.
; Apply positional adjustment, draw the completion pose, clear transient movement state and commit the
; first-side step.
; Mirror first-step setup, selecting state 2 and the corresponding pose.
; Complete the second-side step, clear transient movement state and commit its pose.
; Select mirrored first-side stepping, set motion-side flag, draw the pose and enter state 3.
; Complete state 3 and clear transient movement fields before committing the mirrored pose.
; Select mirrored second-side stepping, draw its pose and enter state 4.
; Complete state 4 and clear transient movement fields before committing the mirrored pose.
; Choose first-side flag, offset state 1 and an animated released-input pose, then commit offset
; collision geometry.
; Choose mirrored flag, offset state 2 and the matching released-input pose.
; Clear continuation and configure paired motion before joining the first-side offset pose path.
; Recompute motion rates, select offset state 5 and draw the first-side pose using the current pose
; offset.
; Clear continuation and configure paired motion before joining the second-side offset pose path.
; Recompute motion rates, select offset state 6 and draw the second-side pose using its offset.
; Clear continuation and select mirrored offset state 3.
; Clear continuation and select mirrored offset state 4.
; Add the configured screen displacement until the player reaches the center; then convert motion to
; scroll unless the endpoint is set. Update course coordinates and terrain response.
; Apply the reverse displacement with a minimum screen coordinate, or convert it to scroll in Dark
; Tunnel; update terrain response.
; Handle the special movement flag, mat pattern and collision response; synchronize an auxiliary
; object position and select its pose.
; When not already in a lane, choose lane 1 and its screen coordinate; update the auxiliary object's
; coordinate too.
; Select lane 2 and its screen coordinate, sharing the same already-in-lane guard.
; Restore the central screen coordinate and clear lateral-lane state.
; Select special pose $13 and animation $42; return the current mat mask for the caller.
; Move the player toward the stored coordinate in six-pixel steps; on arrival clear the continuation
; and feed the default mat pattern back to the dispatcher.
; Count idle frames and penalize prolonged inactivity; otherwise increase the pose offset and
; redispatch by the stored offset-state selector.
; Cancel the stored continuation when mat input changes, otherwise draw the held pose and advance
; rhythm; Dark Tunnel compares old and new masks explicitly.
; Clear offsets, scroll and rhythm, draw the base pose and commit its collision geometry.
; Select a wide/fallback animation by event, reset transient offsets and commit the pose.
; Small repeated movement/property values between code blocks. Boundary and non-code role are
; supported by the earlier slice review; individual meanings and consumer domains remain unresolved.
; Choose scratch $09 from rhythm thresholds and event type; values are 1, 2 or 4. The mat-to-action
; meaning remains tentative.
; Choose scratch $08 from the same rhythm thresholds, for screen-space rather than scroll motion.
; Choose a signed motion rate for the current terrain and side; the mirrored side uses $FC (-4).
; Store A:X as the low/high target-minus-one word and set movement state 5. The dispatcher will push
; it and return through it on a later task visit.
; Account for a collision, play its sound, draw recovery pose and install a timed continuation.
; The installed continuation begins at DrawRecoveryRaisedPose.
; Clear movement state, draw pose $10 thirty-two pixels above PlayerY, and schedule the centered
; recovery pose after six task ticks.
; Draw the same recovery pose at the player coordinates, then wait ten ticks before the final recovery
; delay.
; Wait ten more ticks before dispatching event-specific recovery. Continuations store entry-minus-one
; for the RTS dispatcher.
; Clear movement/continuation state, select an event-specific recovery pose and install its delayed
; continuation.
; Clear movement state. Event 2 goes directly to shared recovery; events below 4 search horizontally
; for a clear collision position, then clamp X to at least $20. Event 4 uses the alternate pose cycle.
; Draw the alternate recovery pose and install a sixteen-tick continuation.
; Run six paired recovery poses, normally $12/$13. StoredPlayerPosition selects alternate pairs for
; two exceptional positions; task delays separate each half-cycle.
; Draw the first selected pose and schedule the second pose after six ticks.
; PlayerCourseSubblock/Pixel temporarily hold animation IDs here.
; Draw the second pose, wait six ticks, and schedule the cycle counter update.
; Clear the stored continuation and movement state. Repeat the pair until six cycles finish, then
; dispatch event-specific terrain recovery.
; Event 2 starts the longer paired recovery; event 4 enters the existing terrain routine. Other events
; adjust the collision position before falling through to the established recovery reset.
; Draw the base pose, synchronize the auxiliary object and install a six-tick continuation.
; Set six paired poses with thirteen ticks per half-cycle. Event zero substitutes poses $5A/$59; the
; other events use $14/$15.
; Draw the first selected recovery pose and install the second-pose continuation.
; Draw the second pose and schedule the counter update after thirteen ticks.
; Repeat until all six pairs finish, then wait ten ticks before restoring player movement.
; Reset movement helpers, optionally reset rafting, clear rhythm/continuation state and seed the
; decoded mat mask. Restore pose and collision-enable fields for normal updates.
; Clamp Hop-a-Log's lateral coordinate before sharing the event-completion path.
; Remove event tasks/sprites, accumulate score, play completion sounds and install a delayed
; continuation. Natural terminal progression remains unverified.
; Clear movement state and build a five-part finish decoration in sixteen-step stages.
; PlayerCourseSubblock/Pixel are temporary Y/X origins and PlayerCourseMajor is the stage counter.
; Move the temporary origin up one pixel and cycle three object animations at sprite slot $24, with
; ten task ticks between poses.
; Draw the next finish pose at the temporary origin and schedule the next counter update.
; Repeat the three poses, move the origin up $20, draw the event-flag-selected final pose and the
; score, then choose sound by score bands below 40, 40..79 and at least 80.
; Start the chosen consecutive audio commands and wait $80 ticks before the player's final pose cycle.
; Clear movement state and enter the score-dependent six-cycle player animation.
; Wait $20 frames, clear player motion, reset movement scratch, and set event flag $40 so the
; lifecycle can leave the event.
; Load event descriptors, initialize scrolling, player coordinates and course counters, then wait for
; the start mat pattern outside demos and install the timed start continuation.
; Draw countdown pose $4C, delay sixteen ticks, and install the countdown repeat check directly as a
; target-minus-one word.
; Count down repeated accents. Once the counter expires, select two more alternations and draw the
; neutral countdown pose.
; Draw pose $4B and schedule the alternate pose after sixteen ticks.
; Draw pose $4D and schedule the next repeat check after sixteen ticks.
; Repeat the neutral/alternate pair until the counter expires, then hold the neutral pose for eighteen
; ticks.
; Draw player pose 1 and enter the staged start decoration. Event 4 first sets SpecialMovementState.
; Clear initialization flag $08, optionally start the event's three-command audio group unless flag
; $80 suppresses it, and enable player collision with $80.
; Five event-indexed starting audio IDs, each starting a three-command group through
; EnableEventMovement. The following five bytes duplicate them; their independent consumer is
; unresolved.
; Choose one of ten event/variant resource sets: collision map, attributes, course indices, tile
; descriptors, block records and strip data; also select CHR and spawn stream.
; Resource arrays used by InitializePlayerEvent and LoadEventResources: five event vertical origins;
; ten start-X/start-Y/end coordinates; seven ten-word pointer arrays; ten CHR selections and collision
; row strides. Variant arrays use index 0..9. Pointer words are CPU addresses in fixed PRG banks.
; Clear rhythm, offsets, recovery flags and movement state without erasing the entire task record.
; Build five decoration parts in sixteen-step stages, with temporary Y starting at $F0 and X at
; PlayerX+$20. Then hold the completed decoration for $40 task ticks.
; Optionally start command $30, draw final object pose $19 at sprite slot $1F and schedule cleanup
; after sixteen ticks.
; Hide twelve sprites from slot $20, wait three frames, then share the initialization finalizer.
; Draw pose $16 at the temporary origin, beginning at sprite slot $1F. The build loops vary temporary
; Y one pixel per step.
; Draw pose $17 at temporary Y minus $10, beginning at sprite slot $21.
; Draw pose $18 at temporary Y minus $20, beginning at sprite slot $24.
; Draw pose $1C at temporary Y minus $20, beginning at sprite slot $24; this is the finish-build
; variant.
; Draw pose $34 at temporary Y minus $30, beginning at sprite slot $2A.
; Draw pose $34 at temporary Y minus $40, beginning at sprite slot $2B.
; Select paired player poses by score band and event flag bit 1, then run six pairs with sixteen ticks
; per pose. The temporary course fields hold the pose IDs.
; Draw the first selected player pose and schedule the second after sixteen ticks.
; Draw the second selected player pose and schedule the cycle update after sixteen ticks.
; Repeat six pose pairs, then jump to the event-animation finalizer.
; Only Rafting uses this auxiliary sprite. Draw when within horizontal bounds; otherwise hide it and
; set an auxiliary state flag.
; Increment an event-selected penalty and additional counters chosen by the current pose/side, then
; cap five counters at 140.
; Unknown physical $34AA..$34AD: bytes encode JMP $B4F0, but no selected jump-stub contract
; distinguishes code from data. Neighboring penalty routines remain supported code.
; Shared penalty branches update different counter combinations, then join the common saturation loop.
; Repeated low-valued rating/penalty selectors used by result and collision accounting. Event-to-
; counter order is table-driven; no semantic names for the five penalties are established.
; Combine capped total score, per-event completion and random low bits, subtract penalties and clamp
; resulting five ratings. No-completion clears all ratings.
; Read a bounded-position spawn record when course progress reaches it; unpack round threshold and
; object type, load task arguments and allocate the object task.
; Subtract signed scroll delta from five active object records and three auxiliary screen coordinates.
; Select an event palette variant from event and round parity, then continue to Rafting decorations
; when appropriate.
; For Rafting, advance three pseudo-randomized positions, draw repeated decorations and selectively
; hide sprites using random state.
; Four-byte rafting decoration descriptor followed by three Y-coordinate bytes. The decoration loop
; uses Y=3..1 with RaftDecorationY as its base, so the base overlaps the descriptor tail and the reads
; address the following three bytes.
; Reset X to $20 and scan Y from $5F through $84 until the collision test clears; otherwise advance X
; and retry. On success advance Y four pixels. This search has no explicit global bound.
; Save the original X in Work0F, then move left until collision clears. Falling below $20 uses the
; full position search; nonzero events subtract four pixels after a successful horizontal search.
; Apply negative scroll while recovery and collision tests permit, then reset recovery and enter the
; auxiliary recovery path.
; While on matching terrain, move the player and draw a recovery pose; otherwise clear recovery and
; install the next delayed continuation.
; Unknown physical $37A9..$37AB: two RTS-valued bytes following a return. Isolated return stubs and
; data remain indistinguishable; no fallthrough or selected entry is established.
; Dark Tunnel alone maps course position through a property table to lateral displacement or a stored
; target coordinate. Other events return zero.
; Dark Tunnel property arrays used after ScreenToCoursePosition. Codes select height/motion cases; the
; later-round table is chosen in mode 2 after a completed round. Precise table extents within this
; data span remain qualified.
; Return carry set only for Dark Tunnel property 1 at the player's current course position.
; Return carry for Dark Tunnel properties 1 or 2, with A distinguishing the two; otherwise return
; zero/carry clear.
; Choose recovery animation and sound by event and collision/terrain status; carry distinguishes the
; alternate recovery form.
; Low-valued motion/property constants adjacent event-dependent recovery tests. Non-code layout is
; established; no finer format is claimed.
; Return carry set for Dark Tunnel and clear for the other events.
; Use course block and subblock position to test Dark Tunnel movement boundaries, with a separate
; later-round property table.
; Subtract A from the base-8 fractional course coordinate when scroll is nonzero; borrow through two
; fractional fields and wrap the major coordinate at 98.
; Add A to the same base-8 coordinate, carrying through both fractions and wrapping the major
; coordinate at 98; refresh the player's derived course position.
; Add screen coordinate A to the base-8 course coordinate. Return major block, subblock and pixel
; remainder in scratch $10/$11/$12.
; Increment the rhythm counter with saturation at 21.
; Derive a task delay from rhythm divided by four, with a minimum delay of one tick.
; Preserve task X. Read collision record Y, add six pixels to its vertical coordinate, and query the
; course bit map using its horizontal coordinate. The caller must restore collision Y afterward.
; Probe the collision bit map at auxiliary coordinates plus an eight-pixel offset.
; Probe below/behind the player using fixed coordinate offsets.
; Select the upper probe coordinate and share the common collision-map query.
; Convert screen coordinates to course block/subblock, select a mask, compute row*map-stride and
; return carry according to the collision bit.
; Select the event/pose-specific collision query; events with offset poses may bypass the normal map
; test.
; If PoseOffsetActive is nonzero return carry clear through the existing bypass. Otherwise set the
; probe row to $80 and fall through to the player-map query with PlayerX in A. Static entry contract;
; natural caller remains unresolved.
; Derive the player course coordinates, account for vertical pose offset, and query the row/bit
; collision map. Rafting has a separate upper probe.
; Eight descending masks ($80 through $01). Collision queries use the course subblock index to select
; one bit in a row byte.
; A selects a three-byte animation record (sprite count and descriptor pointer). Hide the first ten
; sprites, then render the sequence at X/Y origin.
; Same animation record format, but retain existing sprites and offset destination sprite indices by
; the object's base slot.
; Hide Y consecutive sprites starting with index A; preserve the loop count through the shared sprite
; helper.
; Object/property data with repeated low-alphabet layouts. Nearby sprite/collision consumers and
; bounded pattern inspection support non-code; exact subtable schemas and selector bounds remain
; unresolved.
; Initialize the primary object type, task coordinates and sprite allocation before sharing common
; object construction.
; Skip disallowed object/mode combinations, otherwise construct the object selected by the spawn
; record.
; Allocate an eight-byte collision record from the task slot, copy coordinates/type and six property
; bytes, choose randomized motion when needed, then draw the initial animation.
; Object start-sound selectors, indexed by object type. Eight bytes are present; this does not prove
; that every object type is reachable or valid.
; Negative object state takes teardown; otherwise suppress updates during initialization and indirect-
; dispatch by the copied object type. The bounded spawn streams select types 1,2,3,4,6,7; type 0 is
; initialized separately and type 5 shares the type-7 handler. This is a static domain, not an
; assertion that every entry was naturally observed.
; Eight six-byte object property records. Construction copies four motion parameters followed by two
; collision extents. Bounded spawn records select types 1,2,3,4,6,7; startup selects type 0. Type 5
; shares the supported type-7 handler, without an independently observed selector here.
; First object handler word. Type zero is independently installed by task startup, so its dispatch
; contract is established.
; Seven further object handler words complete the eight-entry table. Bounded spawn records, property
; records and coherent task/collision contracts support the targets. The low-nibble mask does not
; establish an additional eight entries.
; Accumulate fractional motion, update the collision coordinate and drain the event score; exhaustion
; marks the event ended and removes the task. Otherwise select animation from score parity.
; Increment the task counter, set collision flags $E0 and integrate both coordinates. Bounds failure
; enters common removal; otherwise select a two-frame animation, with a different counter bit for type
; Set collision flag $40, test horizontal bounds and remove an out-of-range object. Otherwise choose
; among four frames from contact flag, task state and counter, latching state bit $40 on the last
; transition.
; Initialize the object's state, collision flags and $50-tick countdown, then share timed
; motion/contact processing. X is the task offset and Y its eight-byte collision-record offset.
; Contact and event selection can stop motion. A countdown precedes negative vertical speed; afterward
; collision/position tests choose removal, a snapped stationary position or continued acceleration and
; motion.
; When the countdown expires choose signed speed $FB or $FC according to object type, then enter
; acceleration.
; Event 3 can continue upward until the collision coordinate passes the task's saved Y. Event/type and
; course probes choose teardown versus snapping to a row boundary.
; For later events require the contact bit, then snap Y to the sixteen-pixel row base plus ten. Save
; Y/depth, hold forty ticks and clear velocity/fraction state.
; Add $38 to the fractional/integer vertical speed, then integrate both coordinates and test
; horizontal bounds.
; Use contact flags, event-frame parity, object type and signed velocity to select the animation.
; Exact game identity of these objects remains unresolved.
; Increment the phase clock. Initially expose a temporary collision/sprite record and animate using
; type 8's frame table; after eight ticks join timed object motion, while a short descriptor effect
; finishes separately.
; Temporarily use object type 8 to select one of two animation frames, then restore the original type
; and return.
; Advance state, set collision flags, seed the countdown and enter the common timed motion path before
; updating the temporary effect.
; Before phase twenty, draw a selected descriptor at the saved temporary origin; phase nineteen hides
; its sprite and clears temporary flags. Later phases return without drawing.
; CMP #$13 feeds carry into SBC #$09, then mask $0C selects descriptor offsets. Counters 8/9 can
; select offset 12, aliasing following code at UpdateObjectTypes5And7; do not infer an exclusive
